claim: The solar planning case does not fit the interconnection it is designed against. Provo City Code 12.03.080(5) puts standard residential net metering under 25 kW on inverter AC nameplate; the planning case is 40–41 kW AC on 49 kWp DC. `scope` sets the revised target at or below 25 kW AC, and every sizing section under it plans 49 kWp regardless. `customer-generation` names the two ways out — derate the AC side, or take the commercial licence at a worse export credit — and picks neither.

evidence:
Read across the solar thread of `alan/book/pages/my-projects/sections/`, whose sections sit under `book-section/my-projects/solar-power`.

`customer-generation`: "12.03.080(5) classifies licenses under 25 kW as standard net-metering … the Standards document and License Application use **inverter AC nameplate (kW)** as the size field." Then: "**Practical implication for ~50 kWp DC array:** at typical 1.1–1.3 DC/AC ratios this is ~38–45 kW AC, well above the 25 kW residential threshold. **It does not fit standard residential net metering.**" Its two paths: "Reduce inverter AC capacity below 25 kW (oversized DC / clipped AC)" or "the **Commercial Net Metering rate (`NTCR`) at −$0.0453 / kWh**". It closes: "This is a real constraint to bring back to scope."

`scope` took it back: "**System at or below the 25 kW AC residential cap**, unless the commercial path is explicitly chosen. With 1.20 ILR this is ~30 kWp DC", and lists it among the constraints that "shape every downstream sizing decision".

Downstream it vanishes. `pv`: "49 ÷ 1.20 = **41 kW AC**. Round to 40 kW." `topology` sizes the back-fed breaker on it: "At 40 kW AC / 240 V = 167 A". `recommendation`'s bid anchor: "49 kWp … ILR 1.20 → 40 kW AC". None of `sizing`, `pv`, `topology`, `cost` or `recommendation` names the cap; the third of `recommendation`'s numbered priorities is the softer "Provo City Power Schedule 1.1 net-metering details … may impose a cap that re-sizes the project", written as though it were not already found.

Not measured: I did not open the code, the Standards or the rate sheet, so the cap and both rates are as `customer-generation` reports them. Whether a 25 kW-derated build serves the modelled demand is arithmetic nobody in the thread ran, and I did not run it either.
